title: MockSleeper waiters can miss an already-started sleep and hang tests
reasoning: The helper only resumes continuations that are already registered at the exact moment sleep(for:) or sleep(until:) runs. If a background task reaches and completes the mock sleep before the test task calls waitForNextSleep(), the later continuation is appended with no future sleep guaranteed to resume it. That turns a scheduler ordering race into a permanent test hang rather than a deterministic synchronization point.
reproduction: Start a task that calls MockSleeper.sleep(for:), allow it to run before the test awaits waitForNextSleep(), then await waitForNextSleep(); no continuation is resumed unless another sleep happens.
recommendation: Replace the bare continuation list with generation-based waiting, such as a monotonically increasing sleepSequence and a waitForSleep(after:) or waitForSleepCount(atLeast:) helper. Tests should capture the current sequence before starting the producer task or wait for a minimum count, so late registration cannot lose the signal.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing helper is itself used as the synchronization primitive, so a missed wakeup manifests as a timeout or hang. There is no dedicated meta-test covering the late-waiter path.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that performs a sleep before registering a waiter and verifies a new generation/count-based API can observe the completed sleep or fail fast instead of suspending indefinitely.
minimumFixScope: Packages/QuorraCore/Tests/IAMIdentityCenterTests/Stubs/MockSleeper.swift plus call sites that use waitForNextSleep() as a background-task synchronization point.

history.reasoning: Original evidence path still exists, but the quoted nextSleepWaiters implementation is gone. MockSleeper now tracks sleepCount and target-count waiters; sleep(for:) and sleep(until:) call signalSleepWaiters(), which increments the count and resumes waiters whose target count has been reached. waitForSleepCount(atLeast:) returns immediately when the requested count already occurred, so a late waiter does not lose a completed sleep. Current test call sites use waitForSleepCount(atLeast: 1), and MockSleeperTests.waitForSleepCountHandlesLateWaiter covers the late-waiter case by sleeping before registering the waiter. I attempted to run the focused test, but swift test was blocked by the read-only sandbox/xcrun cache permission error, and Xcode RunSomeTests failed before execution due an unrelated AWSConfigINILockTestHelper/main.swift build error.
